html:
The Colony of Virginia was the first lasting English colony in North America, founded at Jamestown in 1607. The map shows it in 1650 and 1700.

Its first years were close to failure: settlers starved and fought the Powhatan Confederacy, whose land they had entered. What saved it was tobacco. After about 1612 a tobacco boom drew a stream of English indentured servants, and the colony spread along the rivers of the Chesapeake. In 1619 it set up the first elected assembly in English America, the House of Burgesses, and the same year the first enslaved Africans arrived. The Crown took direct control in 1624.

In 1676 Bacon's Rebellion of poor settlers burned Jamestown. In the decades after it, planters turned from servants to enslaved Africans, and Virginia became a slave society. The capital moved to Williamsburg in 1699. Virginia was the largest of the colonies of British North America and gave the United States many of its founders, among them Thomas Jefferson.
sum: The Colony of Virginia was the first lasting English colony in North America, founded at Jamestown in 1607. The map shows it in 1650 and 1700.
